sentences.text: Microsteus was a small genus of arthrodire placoderms belonging to the family Selenosteidae.
Fossils of this animal have been found in the Upper Frasnian Kellwasserkalk facies of Germany.
The type species of the genus Microsteus is Microsteus dubius.
The genus Microsteus includes three species: M. dubius, M. angusticeps, and M. gracilis.
The species M. angusticeps and M. gracilis were originally classified in the genus Parawalterosteus.
Microsteus lived during the Frasnian stage, between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
It is debated whether M. angusticeps and M. gracilis are distinct species or should be merged with M. dubius.
